material.description: Ubiquitous Language (P2). Suppressing automatic bundle/runner updates is named no-self-update in the on-disk marker and env (NO_SELF_UPDATE_FILE 'gm-mcp-server.no-self-update' and RUNNER_FREEZE_FILE 'agentplug-runner.no-self-update', GM_MCP_NO_SELF_UPDATE and RUNNER_FREEZE_ENV), in AGENTS.md, and in the self-update verb name. The code names the same concept freeze: selfUpdateFreezeReason and bridgeFreezeReason in gm-mcp/src/self-update.js:48 and gm-mcp/src/release-bridge.js:164, the frozen locals at self-update.js:219 and release-bridge.js:294, and the frozen_by / 'freeze state' output in self-update.js:153 and cli.js:218. Decision recorded: no-self-update is the ubiquitous term because it names the marker and env the operator types. Change: rename the code identifiers to noSelfUpdate* (selfUpdateFreezeReason -> selfUpdateSuppressedReason is NOT the choice; use noSelfUpdateReason, bridgeNoSelfUpdateReason, and frozen -> suppressed) in gm-mcp/src/self-update.js, gm-mcp/src/release-bridge.js and the cli.js help and status text. The wire field frozen_by is a user-visible output key and is NOT renamed here; that choice is a mutable for the user. Witness: grep for freeze in gm-mcp/src returns only frozen_by, and node gm-mcp/src/cli.js self-update-status prints the same reason text as before.

material.detail: Root cause (verified live, not the shell-out hypothesis): walk_posix in rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/code_index.rs is a pure in-process walk over host_fs_readdir. On C:\dev\aloopprime, fs_readdir {"path":"."} lists an entry named `nul`, but fs_stat {"path":"./nul"} returns not-found, because nul is a reserved DOS device name Win32 will not open in any directory. With checked == true walk_posix did `return Err("file stat failed for {next}")`, propagating as file_enumeration_failed / complete:false / enumeration_complete:false -- so one unstattable entry costs the whole project its index and every codeinsight call answers 'symbol index refresh is incomplete' forever. FIX IS WRITTEN BUT NOT LANDED: committed as rs-plugkit 8395d5ebadd008c2c29810024e5a80d7f60248ab (one path, crates/plugkit-core/src/code_index.rs) -- unstattable entries are now skipped and recorded (FileEnumeration::skipped_unstattable surfaced by codeinsight_index) instead of fatal, and Windows reserved device names (con/prn/aux/nul/com1..com9/lpt1..lpt9, case-insensitive, with or without extension, plus trailing-dot/space) are pre-filtered only when the host cwd is Windows-shaped so a POSIX aux.rs still indexes. Compile-verified: cargo build -p rs-plugkit --release --target wasm32-wasip1 --features slim exit 0 (5,656,887-byte wasm). NOT DONE: the wasm was never installed to ~/.agentplug/plugins/gm.wasm, so no live codeinsight verification ran -- reconfirmed 2026-10-10 that C:\dev\aloopprime codeinsight_index {"action":"status"} still returns complete:false / 'file stat failed for ./nul'. PUSH BLOCKED, DO NOT FORCE: rs-plugkit main is not a fast-forward of origin/main and another writer has crates/plugkit-core/src/config_sync.rs dirty with 5082 staged deletions under .agentplug-kv/codeinsight-edges/ -- pulling over that clobbers in-flight work. Landing sequence: wait for that writer, pull, push, rebuild+install gm.wasm, then re-run codeinsight_index sync and codeinsight callers on aloopprime.

Recover with exactly: git_pull {branch:"main"} to fast-forward past the remote's new commit, then git_push {rev:"HEAD"}", and the recovery it names then refused verbatim "worktree or index is not clean, so a pull could clobber uncommitted changes -- refusing exactly as before. Dirty tracked files: .gm/prd.yml, skills/gm-orchestrate/SKILL.md, skills/gm-prd/SKILL.md, ...". The served recovery is unreachable in the normal case: every lane keeps .gm/prd.yml dirty (rows append continuously, and a path-scoped commit cannot include it without allow_foreign_rows), so pull is refused exactly when the recovery commands it. Acceptance: on a repo whose remote moved and whose dirty set is lane-owned, the served recovery ends with the sha pushed -- either git_pull fast-forwards past a dirty set it never touches (stash/restore), or the recovery names the clean-tree step first (path-scoped git_finalize of the dirty tracked files, .gm/prd.yml with allow_foreign_rows) before the pull. Witness: on a repo with a moved remote, dirty .gm/prd.yml and one edited skill, running the served recovery verbatim ends with the sha pushed and ci-status read on it, not with a second refusal.
